# Educational Platform

## Goal

A self-service educational platform that tracks mainstream IT certifications, downloads their public syllabus/objectives, and uses AI to generate a complete course per certification: study content, exercises, and on-demand labs. The student enters their catalog, selects a certification, and has everything ready to study and certify.

**Content is never generated by hand.** The AI builds everything based on the catalog (official syllabus + exercise links + extra metadata). The content is generated once and remains static; it is only regenerated when decided.

## Design Principles

- **Snapshot, No Live Dependency**: The syllabus is downloaded once and remains frozen in the repository. If the certification changes upstream, nothing breaks — a separate process detects the change, and the maintainer decides whether to update.
- **State Lives in Files**: Files (MD + YAML) version-controlled in git. If a regeneration goes wrong, use `git diff` and revert.
- **Generate Once**: Generated content is static for the student. No hot generation or on-the-fly scraping during study.
- **CLI First**: Everything the web interface does can be done via CLI. The web app is just a view of the same file catalog.
- **Separate Roles**: The tracker writes versions, the generator writes content, and the web/CLI only read. They never overwrite each other's domain.

## Architecture — 3 Components

### 1. Catalog Tracker (Scraper — nothing is static)

Principle: **All catalog data is derived from an official scraped source**; nothing is maintained manually (manually only "enriched" with `edited` flag so it is never overwritten). Implemented in `core/tracker.py`:

- `teach tracker sync --provider cncf` — deterministic, without AI: GitHub API calls over `cncf/curriculum`; the date of the last commit of each PDF is the curriculum version; marks `new-version-available` if upstream changed.
- `teach tracker sync --provider lpi --backend <ai>` — scrapes `lpi.org` and AI converts the page into structured updates (level/validity/requires).
- `teach cert snapshot <id> --backend <ai>` — downloads the official objectives (HTML or **PDF**, parsed via `pypdf`) and AI converts them into frozen YAML topics in the MD. Existing statuses are preserved; `--force` to re-snapshot.
- `teach paths generate --backend <ai>` — AI proposes career paths from the catalog (respecting `requires`); paths with `edited: true` (e.g., those encoding scraped data from Kubestronaut/CARE) are never overwritten.
- Runs periodically (cron); never touches generated content — only the catalog, and alerts on changes.

### 2. Generator (AI, on-demand)

Interchangeable backends (`TEACH_BACKEND` / `--backend` / `make generate BACKEND=`):

- **litellm** (default): The LiteLLM proxy already running in the cluster (OpenAI compatible API: `LITELLM_BASE_URL` + `LITELLM_API_KEY` + `LITELLM_MODEL`).
- **claude / codex / gemini / custom**: Local CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, or any custom command via `TEACH_AGENT_CMD`). Workflow: generate locally → review → `make publish` (commit + push to the public repository).

Using catalog metadata (syllabus, exercise links, extra data), the AI plans the learning path for each topic and generates:

- **Text with examples** for the topic, referencing official documentation.
- **Guided exercises**: step-by-step walkthroughs with questions.
- **Lab scripts** (e.g. *break & fix*): breaking a state so the student can fix it.
- **Videos** for the topic (future phase — see Roadmap).
- **Lab definition**: what infrastructure resources are required (for Terraform).

Generator Rules:
- If a syllabus update is accepted, **only changed topics** are regenerated.
- Topics with `status: edited` (manually enriched) **are never overwritten** during regeneration.
- Each generated file records which model/prompt generated it for traceability.
- Generated content is original; always with source attribution. Never copy third-party text literally — the syllabus is the index, the content is ours.

### 3. Web: Public Landing + Paid Study Zone

**Public Landing (no login)** — the landing page is the reference of which IT certifications exist, publishable and indexable:
- Complete certification landscape grouped by category and level, with expirations, dependencies, CARE rules, and curriculum version of each cert.
- Official syllabus for each cert (topics + weights + availability). The internal generation status is not exposed: it is translated to "Available/Coming soon".
- Career paths with dependency graph, Kubestronaut/Golden, and CARE.

**Study Zone (login + paid plan)**:
- Content (theory, exercises, labs) requires session + active subscription (HTTP 402 if unpaid).
- v1: `authenticate()` with admin/admin and `has_subscription()` stub which always approves admin — minimal interfaces to plug real users/OIDC and a payment gateway (Stripe or similar) without touching the rest of the app.
- Reads only pre-generated static files; instant user experience.

## Code Architecture

A single `core` layer (Python) containing all logic, and thin wrappers that only parse arguments/HTTP requests:

```
teach/
  core/          # ALL logic: catalog, certs, generator (LiteLLM), labs
    catalog.py
    certs.py
    generator.py
    labs.py
    auth.py      # authenticate(user, pass) — today admin/admin stub, tomorrow OIDC
  cli.py         # typer  → calls core directly (local files, no API)
  api.py         # FastAPI → calls core; session login; serves web assets
  web/           # static frontend consuming the API
```

- The CLI **does not go through the API**: it operates directly on the same local files.
- FastAPI exposes OpenAPI (`/docs`) automatically → the frontend consumes already documented endpoints.
- Python is more than enough: the API is I/O-bound (reading files + waiting for LLM/Terraform); 10k req/h ≈ 2.8 req/s, <1% capacity of a single uvicorn process. The student path serves pre-generated static content — as cheap as possible.

### Decoupled Lab Runner (Future, Go)

Infrastructure execution is decoupled from the Python core via a **declarative contract**:

```
teach/core (Python)          lab-runner (Go, decoupled)
  generates content      →      reads lab specs
  writes lab specs       →      runs terraform (up/down)
  reads lab status       ←      writes status (running/failed/destroyed)
        └── contract: lab.yaml + terraform files + status.yaml ──┘
```

- v1: `core/labs.py` runs Terraform via subprocess (single-user). The contract (lab spec + status) is defined from day one.
- In production: a Go runner (`terraform-exec` by HashiCorp) works against the same contract; the core stops executing and only reads status. Candidate to become a Kubernetes operator in the cluster.
- Communication phases: (a) shared files, (b) runner mini HTTP API, (c) queue (NATS/Redis) under high volume.

## Languages

Supported languages: **es (default), en, fr, de, zh, ja, pt**.

- Content by language: `certs/<cert>/<topic>/<lang>/{content,exercises,meta}`. The **lab configuration is shared** across languages (spec/terraform/scripts).
- `teach cert generate <cert> --lang en` generates in that language; availability per language = file existence (the API exposes `langs` per topic).
- The MD `status` follows the default language.
- API: `?lang=` parameter in content and preview endpoints, with **fallback to Spanish** (marked with `lang_fallback` and warning displayed on the web).
- Web: Language selector in the header (persisted in localStorage, browser language detection); UI translated to all 7 languages.
- Pending: Generate translations for existing content (`--lang en`, etc.).

## Data Model

`catalog.yaml` — the global catalog:

```yaml
certs:
  lpi-010-160:
    name: LPI Linux Essentials
    tracked_version: "1.6"
    upstream_status: current | new-version-available
    sources:
      objectives: https://www.lpi.org/our-certifications/exam-010-objectives/
```

One markdown file per certification, with YAML frontmatter — the generic skeleton mapping any cert:

```markdown
---
cert: lpi-linux-essentials
exam: "010-160"
version: "1.6"
sources:
  - https://www.lpi.org/our-certifications/exam-010-objectives/
  - https://learning.lpi.org/en/learning-materials/010-160/
topics:
  - id: "1.1"
    title: "Linux Evolution and Popular Operating Systems"
    weight: 2
    sources: [...]        # topic-specific links, manually enrichable
    status: generated | edited | stale
---
```

Source links change by topic; they can be enriched manually and the course can be regenerated without losing those links.

## CLI

```
teach cert add lpi-010-160        # downloads and freezes the syllabus (snapshot)
teach cert diff lpi-010-160       # shows what changed upstream vs my snapshot
teach cert update lpi-010-160     # accepts new version (topic by topic)
teach cert generate lpi-010-160   # generates content via LiteLLM (respects edited)
teach lab up lpi-010-160/1.2      # spins up the topic lab
teach lab down lpi-010-160/1.2
teach serve                       # starts the web app over the same catalog
```

## Labs

- Topic labs with **Terraform**, connectable to different targets: clouds, on-prem (Proxmox, libvirt/baremetal) or local machine.
- v1: **Single provider** (cheapest to test: local machine with libvirt, or Proxmox). The lab contract (resources + setup script) is defined in the topic MD; adding providers later is mechanical.
- Lab types: *break & fix* (scripts that break the environment, student fixes it) and guided (guided steps with questions).

### Execution Modes + Exercise Videos (SDD — evaluation, pending implementation)

Evaluation of how to grant lab access (free vs paid) and how to display the solved exercise in a video, to iterate. Starting point: `lab.yaml` (declarative spec per topic) and `break_fix.sh` (actual script, generated and reviewed) already exist; `labs.py` only implements the `terraform` provider, the `local` provider is declared but not implemented.

**Exercise Video — Actual Capture, No Mock.** Same principle as the marketing video (factual data is never written by AI — see the path scene in `core/video.py`): spin up the actual container from `lab.yaml`, run `break_fix.sh` for real, and record the session using **asciinema** (`.cast` file, text format, KB not MB, reproducible/scalable, self-hostable player) instead of mocking the terminal with AI or rendering MP4. The AI only writes the voiceover narration (Piper TTS, as already done).

**Free — Local Docker.** Fills the gap for the `local` provider: generate a deterministic `Dockerfile`/`docker-compose.yml` from `lab.yaml` and the student runs it locally. Cost/risk to the platform: zero. The same container "toolbox" is used to record the asciinema above.

**Paid A — BYO-Cloud + Terraform.** Extends the existing contract in `labs.py` (`up`/`down` over `lab/terraform/`): generate the Terraform module per topic, v1 has the student running `terraform apply` using their own credentials (the platform never touches them). A "one-click" mode where the platform runs Terraform with credentials pasted by the student is more convenient but turns the platform into a custodian of third-party cloud credentials — defer until proven demand.

**Paid B — Hosted by Me, "Connect" Button → Auto-destruction.**
Main risk: the platform runs on a home cluster, publicly exposed. **Do not run third-party labs there** — direct blast radius to the home LAN (lab escape, mining, lateral movement). Alternative: ephemeral VM per session in a separate, cheap cloud provider (Hetzner/DO, billing per minute) using the same "toolbox" image, hard timeout (30-60 min), concurrent session limits, web terminal via xterm.js+websocket, and `terraform destroy` upon session close. Also evaluate existing ephemeral sandboxes (E2B, Coder, Gitpod) before building custom isolation hardening.

**Suggested Order**: Local Docker (reuses existing work, zero risk) → Asciinema video of the same lab → Terraform self-service BYO-Cloud → Hosted ephemeral VM (at the end, only when revenue justifies security investment).

## Levels, Expirations and Career Paths

Official documentation data (lpi.org, cncf.io, docs.linuxfoundation.org):

**LPI** — 3 tracks:
- *Essentials* (no prerequisites, **never expire**): Linux Essentials 010, Security Essentials 020, Web Development Essentials 030, Open Source Essentials 050.
- *Professional* (**5 years**, chain of active prerequisites): LPIC-1 → LPIC-2 → LPIC-3 (300 Mixed Env / 303 Security / 305 Virtualization / 306 High Availability).
- *Open Technology* (**5 years**, no prerequisites): DevOps Tools Engineer 701, BSD Specialist 702.

**CNCF / Linux Foundation**:
- *Associate* (**3 years**): KCNA, KCSA, CGOA, CAPA, CBA, CNPA, CCA, ICA, KCA, OTCA, PCA.
- *Professional* (**2 years** starting 2024-04): CKA, CKAD, CKS (requires active CKA), CNPE.
- **Linux Foundation** (own track, separated from LPI): LFCA (associate, 2 years, 6 domains) → LFCS (professional, 2 years, 5 domains, hands-on exam; required for Golden Kubestronaut). **LFCE retired in 2022 and LFCT retired in 2025** — do not catalog.

**Programs** (all certs must be active at the same time; once all are approved, CNCF contacts by email within a business week):
- **Kubestronaut**: CKA + CKAD + CKS + KCNA + KCSA.
- **Golden Kubestronaut**: All 15 CNCF certs + LFCS. Lifetime title.

**CARE Program** (Certification Advancement & Recertification Experience, active since 2026-01-01, expanded 2026-06-17): Passing/recertifying a higher exam renews lower certifications, matching their expiration dates:
- CKA or CKAD → renews KCNA.
- CKS → renews KCSA.
- CKS → restores and extends CKA, even if already expired (since 2026-06-18).
With CARE, 3 exams (CKS + CKAD + one associate) maintain the 5 Kubestronaut certs. In `catalog.yaml`: `renewed_by` field per cert + `care` entry in paths.

**CNCF "Current" Versioning**: PDFs without semantic versioning are versioned by the **date of the last change to the PDF in git** (`curriculum_updated` field; the tracker monitors commits to the `cncf/curriculum` repo). CKA/CKAD/CKS also carry their own version mapping Kubernetes (v1.35 = K8s 1.35).

All this lives in `catalog.yaml`: `level`, `validity`, `requires` per cert, and a `paths` section (career paths with steps + achievements with `requires_all`). The web interface groups by category → level and displays a "Career Paths" view with the dependency graph.

## Catalog by Categories

The main page groups by category (`category` in `catalog.yaml`):

- **Linux Courses**: Full LPI track — Essentials (010/020/021), LPIC-1, LPIC-2, LPIC-3 (300/303/305/306), DevOps Tools Engineer.
- **Cloud Native (CNCF)**: The 15 certs from `https://github.com/cncf/curriculum` (CKA, CKAD, CKS, KCNA, KCSA, CGOA, CAPA, CBA, CNPA, CNPE, CCA, ICA, KCA, OTCA, PCA). That repository is the source of truth: a versioned PDF per cert (e.g. CKA v1.35), licensed under **CC-BY 4.0**, and CNCF explicitly invites training providers to align classes to the curriculum. The tracker monitors this repo for new PDF versions.
- All loaded with empty syllabus skeleton (`topics: []`); the snapshot of objectives for each cert is frozen when starting course generation. For CNCF, the syllabus is parsed from the PDF (extracting topics + weights).

## First Test Version

First real example: **LPI Linux Essentials (010-160)**

- https://www.lpi.org/
- https://www.lpi.org/our-certifications/linux-essentials-overview/
- https://www.lpi.org/our-certifications/exam-010-objectives/
- https://learning.lpi.org/en/learning-materials/010-160/

Note: LPI learning materials are under Creative Commons — check the license of each source before using as reference.

## Roadmap

1. Data skeleton (catalog.yaml + MD files with frontmatter) with LPI 010-160 as the first real case.
2. CLI: `cert add` + `cert generate` against LiteLLM (text + exercises + break & fix scripts).
3. Version Tracker (`cert diff` / `cert update`) as a periodic cron.
4. `lab up/down` with a single provider.
5. Web interface with admin/admin login stub reading the same catalog.
6. Topic-specific video (requires a separate pipeline from LLM text — e.g. script generation + TTS + slides).
7. Multilingual support (en/es/fr/de/zh/ja/pt): content under `<topic>/<lang>/`, status by language, web selector.
   - Improve web presentation: currently displays raw content; needs Markdown rendering, styles, navigation. (low priority).
8. Go lab-runner, real user authentication, multiple lab providers.
